sessions.phase_label: Compression Springs copy scope and draft delivery
Copy feedback, process alignment, and next landing-page assignment

requirements.title: Expanded Compression Springs Landing-Page Copy
requirements.definition: Produce substantially expanded copy for the Compression Springs landing page according to the supplied outline, excluding separately managed sections.
requirements.boundary_note: Covers the overall expanded page-copy deliverable. The Case Study and Innovation and Customization sections are separate because their ownership and content dependencies evolve independently.

requirements.title: Compression Springs Case Study Section Copy
requirements.definition: Provide copy for the Case Study section identified in the Compression Springs outline.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separate because the client explicitly reassigns this section to its own team while the rest of the landing-page copy remains in scope.

requirements.title: Innovation and Customization Section Copy
requirements.definition: Provide copy for the Innovation and Customization in Spring Manufacturing section using additional Century Spring context.
requirements.boundary_note: Kept separate from core page copy because it has its own source-information dependency and remains pending while the Case Study section is reassigned.

requirements.title: Formal Product-Page Tone
requirements.definition: Use a formal tone on product-information pages, with fewer interjections and exclamation points.
requirements.boundary_note: This is a cross-page editorial constraint that can change independently of any individual landing-page deliverable.

requirements.title: Torsion Springs Landing-Page Copy
requirements.definition: Produce copy for the Torsion Springs landing page using substantially the same scope and outline pattern as the prior Compression Springs assignment, with the requested one-week delivery window.
requirements.boundary_note: This is an independent page deliverable. Its delivery window and inherited scope are attributes of the assignment rather than separate Requirements.
